en: 7. The Chapter on the Arising of Underlying Tendencies (Anusaya-yamaka) 7.1. Section on the Basis of Arising.
Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One.

The underlying tendencies (*anusaya*) are: the underlying tendency to sensual lust (*kāmarāgānusaya*), the underlying tendency to aversion (*paṭighānusaya*), the underlying tendency to conceit (*mānānusaya*), the underlying tendency to views (*diṭṭhānusaya*), the underlying tendency to doubt (*vicikicchānusaya*), the underlying tendency to lust for existence (*bhavarāgānusaya*), and the underlying tendency to ignorance (*avijjānusaya*).
Where does the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlie? In the two types of feeling within the sense-sphere realm (*kāmadhātu*), there the underlying tendency to sensual lust underlies.
Where does the underlying tendency to aversion underlie? In painful feeling, there the underlying tendency to aversion underlies.

Where does the underlying tendency to conceit lie latent? In the two feelings of the sense-sphere realm, and in the form-sphere and formless-sphere realms—here the underlying tendency to conceit lies latent.
Where does the underlying tendency to views lie latent? In all phenomena included within the five aggregates of clinging—here the underlying tendency to views lies latent.
Where does the underlying tendency to doubt lie latent? In all phenomena included within the five aggregates of clinging—here the underlying tendency to doubt lies latent.

Where does the underlying tendency to lust for existence (bhavarāgānusaya) lie latent? In the form element (rūpadhātu) and the formless element (arūpadhātu), there the underlying tendency to lust for existence lies latent.
Where does the underlying tendency to ignorance (avijjānusaya) lie latent? In all phenomena included within the personal aggregates (sakkāya), there the underlying tendency to ignorance lies latent.
This is the section on the bases of arising.
